rows.speaker: الرازي
rows.claim: Razi answers why some surahs open with letters: a surah mentioning the Qurʾān alerts to the whole Qurʾān.
rows.anchor: وقد رد الرازي على الأول، بأن السورة التي فيها ذكر القرآن تُنبه على كل القرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Author finds Razi's answers unconvincing and strained.
rows.anchor: ولا يبدو ردهُّ مقنعاً، بل هو واضح التكلف.

rows.speaker: الزركشي
rows.claim: Zarkashi's approach is clearer: after letter-openings the Qurʾān usually mentions itself; al-ʿAnkabut and al-Rum are exceptions that need explaining.
rows.anchor: وكان "الزركشي" أوضح مسلكاً وأنأى عن تكليف

rows.speaker: الحافظ ابن كثير
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir, by induction, concludes every letter-opened surah must mention defending the Qurʾān and its inimitability.
rows.anchor: فهداه الاستقراء إلى أن كل سورة افتتحت بالحروف فلابد أن يذكر فيها الانتصار للقرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Author says the waw of oath, in its place, marks the surah's opening as an assertion or testimony to what was denied.
rows.anchor: فإذا جاءت للقسم فإن لها الصدارة، في مقام التوثيق لما يسبق إنكاره، أو الإقرار والشهادة

rows.speaker: المفسرون
rows.claim: Exegetes, mostly, read the oath-waw as glorifying the sworn-by object.
rows.anchor: وقد اتجه بها المفسرون، أو جمهرتهم فيما أعلم، إلى تعظيم المقسَم به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Author rejects the exegetes' glory-by-wisdom reasoning and their neglect of the qualifiers attached to the sworn-by object.
rows.anchor: وأما العظمة فلا يهون القول بها لمجرد لمح وجهٍ لظاهر الحكمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Exegetes often ignore the qualifier of the sworn-by object (e.g. the dawn-times of al-Duha).
rows.anchor: ثم إنهم غالباً، لم يراعوا القيد في المقسم به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Author asks how the sworn things relate to their answers, e.g. swift steeds and human ingratitude (kanud), or night and the diversity of human effort.
rows.anchor: فأين الصلة بين عظمة العاديات ضبحاً، وبين كنود الإنسان لربه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Author asks whether the oath-waw form, versus explicit aqsama, adds any rhetorical meaning.
rows.anchor: فهل العدول عن: أقسم بالنجم، إلى "والنجم" لا يعطى أي ملحظ بياني؟

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: All surahs opening with the oath-waw, including al-ʿAsr, are Meccan; no Medinan surah begins this way.
rows.anchor: وكلها سور مكية، ولم تأت سورة مدنية مبدوءة بهذه الواو.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In al-ʿĀdiyāt the waw recalls known raids and prepares for the unseen resurrection and the exposure of hearts; the human is ungrateful to his Lord.
rows.anchor: السورة تبدأ بالواو لافتة إلى ما عهد القوم من غارات الخيل المصبحة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In al-ʿAsr the waw places the human under the pressure of time, which squeezes and tests him.
rows.anchor: الواو في موضعها الذي تطرد به الظاهرة الأسلوبية في اللفت إلى ابتلاء الإنسان بالزمن يعصره ويصهره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Time's pressing extracts the human's essence, revealing whether his outcome is loss or salvation (exempting those who believe and do good and counsel truth and patience).
rows.anchor: توطئة إيضاحية لبيان ما يستخلص العصرُ من عصارة هذا الإنسان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the verse al-ʿaṣr means time (zaman, dahr); the word is a single-form Qurʾānic usage here.
rows.anchor: العَصْر، بمعنى الزمن، في آية العصر

rows.speaker: نافع
rows.claim: Nafiʿ asked about al-muʿṣirāt (78:14); the answer given: clouds press one another so water comes out between them.
rows.anchor: وسأل نافع عن قوله تعالى: {وَأَنْزَلْنَا مِنَ الْمُعْصِرَاتِ}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Author sees no need to restrict al-muʿṣirāt to two clouds; the explanation is a gloss.
rows.anchor: ولا نرى ضرورة لقيد المعصرات بسحابتين

rows.speaker: الراغب
rows.claim: Author rejects Raghib's derivation of time from the residue of what is pressed.
rows.anchor: وأخذه "الراغب" من نفاية ما يُعصَر. وليس الوجه.

rows.speaker: الراغب
rows.claim: Raghib does not restrict to two clouds; he explains muʿṣirāt as clouds pressed by rain, and others say they bring the storm.
rows.anchor: و"الراغب" لم يحدد سحابتين، بل فسر المعصرات بالسحائب التي تعتصر بالمطر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Author rejects the view that muʿṣirāt bring the storm (iʿṣār), since the context of the verse and Qurʾānic usage do not support it.
rows.anchor: وما نقله في المعصرات من قولٍ بأنها تأتي بالإعصار، لا يؤنس إليه سياق الآية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The root ʿ-ṣ-r points to pressing to extract juice; the sense of time (dahr) is named for extracting man's essence through trial.
rows.anchor: وتسمية الدهر عصراً، ملحوظ فيه أنه يستخلص عصارة الإنسان بالضغط والابتلاء والمعاناة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: General root meaning of ʿ-ṣ-r is pressing for juice, used literally of grapes and metaphorically of wine.
rows.anchor: والعصر في كل صيغة واستعماله، يرجع إلى أصل دلالته على الضغط لاستخلاص العصارة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas, asked by Nafiʿ, glosses ʿaḍud as helper.
rows.anchor: فقال ابن عباس: العضد، المعين الناصر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The root of iʿṣār (a whirlwind with fire in 2:266) relates to pressing; the wind-sense is close to the root's sense of squeezing.
rows.anchor: وتفسير الإعصار بالريح الشديدة، قريب، مع ملحظ دلالة مادته على

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word ʿaṣr meaning time occurs in 103:1, alongside al-muʿṣirāt (78:14) and the verbs in Yusuf.
rows.anchor: والمعصرات فى آية النبأ 14، والعصر بمعنى الدهر والزمن فى آية العصر

rows.speaker: الجوهري
rows.claim: Jawhari defines iʿṣār as a wind raising dust that rises like a column.
rows.anchor: وقال الجوهرى: والإعصار ريح تهب تثير الغبار

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas, via a chain the author notes from Tabari, glosses iʿṣār as a wind carrying hot poison.
rows.anchor: أسند عن ابن عباس، قال: ريح فيها سموم شديدة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses muraghaman as open space (manfasihan), in the dialect of Hudhayl, citing a poet.
rows.anchor: فقال ابن عباس: منفسحْا، بلغة هذيل

rows.speaker: كثير منهم
rows.claim: Many readers of Hamza, Abu ʿAmr, Ibn ʿĀmir, Yaʿqub or Warsh choose a pause (sakt) between al-ʿAsr and Wayl li-kull humazah (104:1).
rows.anchor: وبين والعصر، وويل لكل همزة

rows.speaker: كثير منهم
rows.claim: Many of them choose basmala in these four places, since uncovered sequences like wayl after a word would sound harsh.
rows.anchor: اختار كثير منهم لهم البسملة في هذه الأربعة المواضع

rows.speaker: الأكثرون
rows.claim: Most scholars make no distinction between these four places and others; Dani and the verifiers hold this.
rows.anchor: والأكثرون على عدم التفرقة بين الأربعة وغيرها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Author prefers no distinction among the four places, the view of Abu ʿAmr al-Dani and the verifiers.
rows.anchor: وهو اختيار أبي عمرو الداني والمحققين، والله تعالى أعلم

rows.speaker: أكثر الفقهاء
rows.claim: Most jurists: standing at Arafat begins after noon and ends at night, so the standing is partly by day and partly by night.
rows.anchor: فابتداء الوقوف بالنهار، وآخره بالليل، هذا قول أكثر الفقهاء

rows.speaker: مالك بن أنس
rows.claim: Malik holds the time of standing is at night; standing only by day is not valid.
rows.anchor: وحكي عن مالك بن أنس أن وقت الوقوف بالليل، وإن لم يقف ليلا لم يجز

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Author prefers the first view (standing by day and night), which the Sunna supports.
rows.anchor: والأول هو الصحيح، وتدل عليه السنة

rows.speaker: أبو حنيفة
rows.claim: Abu Hanifa: the Imam is a condition for the rites, and the place too; Abu Yusuf and Muhammad disagree on the Imam.
rows.anchor: والإمام شرط في الجميع عند أبي حنيفة

rows.speaker: أبو يوسف ومحمد
rows.claim: Abu Yusuf and Muhammad hold that the Imam is not a condition.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو يوسف ومحمد: ليس بشرط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pre-Islamic Arabs left Arafat before sunset and Muzdalifa after sunrise, saying 'the peak should shine'; the Prophet ordered the opposite.
rows.anchor: وكان أهل الجاهلية يدفعون عن عرفة قبل غروب الشمس

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: The Prophet ordered his community to act against the pre-Islamic departure practice.
rows.anchor: فأمر النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم - بمخالفتهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse shows that knowing the rites is not a necessity, as 2:198 says 'and you were before it among the astray'.
rows.anchor: وتدل على أن المعارف ليست ضرورة؛ لذلك قال

rows.speaker: أبو حنيفة
rows.claim: Abu Hanifa: standing at Muzdalifa is obligatory, not a pillar; leaving it requires a sacrifice; the verse indicates it.
rows.anchor: فقال أبي حنيفة: واجب إن تركه فعليه دم، وليس بركن، وتدل الآية عليه

rows.speaker: الليث
rows.claim: Layth holds standing at Muzdalifa is a pillar.
rows.anchor: وعن الليث أنه ركن

rows.speaker: الشافعي
rows.claim: Shafiʿi: if one departs in the last half of the night there is no fault; for the first half there are two views.
rows.anchor: إن دفع في النصف الأخير من الليل فلا شيء عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zarkashi: al-ʿAsr is counted as a verse by analogy with al-Fajr and al-Duha for the shared rhyme, though their lengths differ.
rows.anchor: للمناسبة لكن تفاوتت فى الكمية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zarkashi lists al-ʿAsr among the fifteen surahs opened by an oath.
rows.anchor: ﴿ والعاديات ﴾ ﴿ والعصر ﴾ فتلك خمس عشرة سورة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zarkashi counts seven surahs opened by a conditional (ʾidhā-type) construction.
rows.anchor: ﴿ إذا جاء نصر الله ﴾ فذلك سبع سور

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Zamakhshari: verse-division is tawqifi (by transmission), with no room for analogy.
rows.anchor: وقال الزمخشرى الآيات علم توقيف لا مجال للقياس فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A single word can be an ayah, such as al-Fajr, al-Duha and al-ʿAsr.
rows.anchor: وقد تكون الكلمة آية مثل ﴿ والفجر ﴾ ﴿ والضحى ﴾ ﴿ والعصر ﴾

rows.speaker: القاضي أبو بكر بن العربي
rows.claim: Ibn al-ʿArabi: verse-counting should rely on the practice of the early generation.
rows.anchor: وينبغى أن يعول فى ذلك على فعل السلف

rows.speaker: أبو عمرو الداني
rows.claim: Dani knows of no single word that is an ayah except mudhāmmatān in al-Rahman.
rows.anchor: لا أعلم كلمة هى وحدها آية إلا قوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zarkashi lists al-ʿAsr among the surahs containing both an abrogating and an abrogated verse, along with al-Muzzammil, al-Muddaththir, al-Takwir.
rows.anchor: والمزمل والمدثر والتكوير والعصر

rows.speaker: ابن العربي
rows.claim: Ibn al-ʿArabi notes a rare verse whose first part is abrogated and last part abrogates, the verse of 'you are responsible for yourselves'.
rows.anchor: ذكره ابن العربي في أحكامه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abrogation of recitation with the ruling kept: the old text on stoning the married adulterer, accepted by the community.
rows.anchor: الأول ما نسخ في تلاوته وبقي حكمه فيعمل به إذا تلقته الأمة بالقبول

rows.speaker: عمر
rows.claim: Umar said that if people did not say he added to the Qurʾān he would have written the stoning verse himself.
rows.anchor: لولا أن يقول الناس زاد عمر في كتاب الله
